description.narrative: A trust fund with European Investmetn Bank established and its credit programme for water/waste Water projects in 40 BiH municipalities be supported by grant money for investment and TA.
A trust fund with European Investmetn Bank established and its credit programme for water/waste Water projects in 40 BiH municipalities be supported by grant money for investment and TA.

The Project concerns establishment of co-financing arrangement for municipal infrastructure projects with the European Investment Bank (EIB), with the main components: a) institutional capacity building of waste water utilities in the areas of operational efficiency and sustainability b) selective investments to the highly needed waste water treatment facilities. The overall aim of the Project is to provide improved municipal environmental infrastructure services to BiH citizens in accordance with EU directives, leading to improved environment and health. The result of the Project will be that participating municipal utilities will move towards compliance with EU-regulations on higher quality, reliability and sustainability of services, decrease environmental pollution and increase energy efficiency through a series of institutional improvements and selective investments in rehabilitation and wastewater systems. Sida contribution will be used to expand the ongoing water and sanitation programme financed from the EIB loan, EU grants and local contribution.

sector.narrative: Water supply and sanitation - large systems

description.narrative:
The overview of achievements and related challenges in 2025 is presented below:
Municipality of Tomislavgrad: Design and construction of Waste Water Treatment Plant (WWTP). The water supply, collection and treatment project of the municipality of Tomislavgrad consists of (i) Component A related to water supply system and (ii) wastewater collection and WWTP. All components have been completed in 2025. The Municipality conducted Technical inspection of WWTP in October 2025 and after that issued Usage Permit in December 2025, since when WWTP is up and running.
Municipality of Bosanski Petrovac, Waste Water Treatment Plant (WWTP). The water collection and treatment project of the municipality of Bosanski Petrovac consists of (i) Construction of sewers East and Central area and (ii) Design and construction of the WWTP. While the first component has been completed, the construction of the WWTP (financed by Sida) is still under construction. Considering that 90% of the works have been completed, it is foreseen that the contracted works could be substantially completed by the end of February 2026 (without testing and commissioning), which will require an additional period of 3 months. It is estimated that the Sida funds will be utilized by 30 June 2026. This will be followed up by EIB separately, as annual report covers period Jan-Dec 2025.
Municipality of Trebinje: the WWTP is completed, including the procurement and installation of the additional sludge treatment equipment which was finalized in June 2024
Municipality of Teslic: the WWTP works are fully completed in 2023
City of Mostar: Works on tunnel and syphon were completed in 2021
Generally, key challenge in implementation was the delayed extension of the Contract for Supervision Services, financed outside Sida grant, which consequently caused further delays in implementation in FBIH. To accommodate this delay, which is out of control of EIB and municipalities, EIB requested yet another no-cost extension which has been approved by Sida.
In summary:
Municipality of Mostar: works were completed and unused funds have been reallocated; Municipality of Tomislavgrad: works were completed in 2025. Municipality of Bosanski Petrovac: The final completion is foreseen by end of May 2026 (to be additionaly followed up with EIB); Municipality of Trebinje: all works are completed; Municipality of Teslic: the WWTP works are fully completed.
Overall achievement: Finalizing construction of Waste water treatment facilities at local level (within this and other projects funded by Sida and implemented by IFIs like EBRD, EIB, WB) and having them operational will help Bosnia and Herzegovina to comply with the EU Directive of Urban Waste Water even in absence of the countrywide water&waste water strategy. New WWTPs constructed in BIH in last 10 years contributed to increasing the percentage of treated waste water discharged into recipients (rivers) from 1,5% in 2014 to estimated 22% in 2025 making BIH more compliant with EU requirements and reducing organic pollution in the rivers. These constructions were very often supported by Sweden in cooperation with IFIs, such as EIB (this project), EBRD, WB but also by other donors (EU, Swiss/SECO, CZ) or Banks (KFW).
